channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Youth Protests in France Spread to Belgium, Sparking Clashes
item.description: Clashes erupted in central Brussels between police and masked youths, with hundreds throwing objects at officers. The unrest occurred during a general strike against government austerity plans. Protests are linked to student dissatisfaction over education reforms, including tuition hikes and budget cuts, with over 100 arrests in Liege.

item.title: ADB Grants $1 Million for "Green" Energy Corridor Project Involving Uzbekistan
item.description: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) has allocated a $1 million grant for the initial phase of the "Caspian Green Energy Corridor" project. This project aims to connect the energy systems of Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, and Azerbaijan. The grant will fund the feasibility study for a subsea cable between Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan, with Uzbekistan connecting via land networks.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans Over 100 Events During CIS Presidency
item.description: During its upcoming presidency of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), Uzbekistan plans to implement over 100 events. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev emphasized focusing on practical results, removing trade barriers, utilizing Central Asia's transport potential, and strengthening scientific ties. The presidency's concept and action plan are nearing completion.

item.title: ExxonMobil Blocks $5 Billion Settlement Deal Over Sulfur Fine in Kazakhstan
item.description: ExxonMobil has blocked a proposed $5 billion settlement with Kazakhstan regarding a fine for excess sulfur storage at the Kashagan field. According to Bloomberg, ExxonMobil disagreed with the terms of the settlement, preventing the North Caspian Operating Company consortium from reaching an agreement with Kazakh authorities. Other partners like Shell and TotalEnergies initially favored the settlement.

item.title: Navi Pillay Awarded 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for Human Rights Advocacy
item.description: Navi Pillay, a South African jurist and former UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, has been awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize. The Norwegian Nobel Committee recognized her efforts in promoting peace and international law. Pillay has a history of fighting apartheid and advocating against torture.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Lawmakers Debate Punishment for Sexual Abuse of Minors Amid Public Outcry
item.description: Following public testimonies of sexual abuse, Kyrgyzstani lawmakers are debating penalties for those convicted of sexual offenses against minors. Numerous citizens have shared their experiences of abuse on social media, highlighting a systemic issue that has prompted parliamentary discussion on stricter legal measures.

item.title: Organizers of Illegal Gold Mining Convicted in East Kazakhstan Region
item.description: Two individuals have been sentenced to four years in prison in Ust-Kamenogorsk for organizing illegal gold mining in the Shybyn'dy area. The operation, conducted through a company with only an exploration license, resulted in over 15 kilograms of gold extracted, causing significant environmental damage estimated at over 300 million tenge for restoration.

item.title: Rural Akim Held Accountable for Illegally Assisting an Entrepreneur
item.description: A rural district akim in the Akmola region has been administratively charged for illegally interfering in a public procurement tender. The akim provided unauthorized assistance to an entrepreneur, violating the entrepreneur's rights and hindering an investment project. The court annulled the tender results.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Payment Balance Shows Surplus for First Time in Three Years
item.description: Kazakhstan's current account of the payment balance turned positive in the first half of 2026, with a surplus of $2.4 billion, or 1.6% of GDP, according to the National Bank. This improvement is mainly due to faster export growth compared to imports. The trade balance surplus doubled.

item.title: Analyst Explains Tokayev's Strategy: 'Trade, Not War'
item.description: Political analyst Abishev explained that President Tokayev's emphasis on developing international transport routes, including connecting the Middle Corridor and TRIPP corridor, signifies Kazakhstan's commitment to a multi-vector foreign policy. This strategy prioritizes long-term economic rationality over geopolitical entanglements, maintaining openness to various routes, including the North-South corridor with Russia.

item.title: Youth Employment and Development Issues Discussed in Karakalpakstan
item.description: Officials in the Republic of Karakalpakstan met with unemployed youth and activists to discuss employment opportunities and support for their initiatives. Meetings are held regularly to gather youth ideas and support their projects, fostering professional and personal growth. The President's attention to youth education and opportunities in Karakalpakstan was highlighted.

item.title: School Student Fatally Stabbed by Classmate in Zhetysu Region
item.description: A tragic incident occurred in the Zhetysu Region where a school student died after being stabbed by a classmate during an argument. The suspect has been apprehended and a criminal case for murder of a minor has been initiated. Additionally, a criminal case has been opened against school staff for failing to ensure the safety and well-being of the children.

item.title: Teenager Detained in Zhetisu Region on Suspicion of Classmate's Murder
item.description: A teenage boy has been detained in the Zhetisu region of Kazakhstan on suspicion of murdering his eighth-grade classmate. The incident occurred after a conflict between students. Police have opened a criminal case for murder and are also investigating school staff for negligence in ensuring child safety. The suspect has been apprehended.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Retain Cash Payments for State Services Amid Digitalization Push
item.description: Kazakhstan will continue to allow cash payments for state services despite the widespread adoption of cashless transactions. Vice Minister of Finance Asset Tursunov stated that while non-cash payments are encouraged and promoted by the National Bank and the Ministry of Finance, citizens retain the right to pay in cash. The government aims to stimulate cashless methods but respects individual choice.

item.title: Fergana Oil Refinery Not Slated for Reprivatization, State Assets Agency Reports
item.description: The State Assets Management Agency announced that the Fergana Oil Refinery is not currently scheduled for reprivatization. The agency's director, Sohibjon Murodov, stated that the company's debts are being reviewed as part of an international audit. Production volumes have increased significantly, with diesel fuel output up 30% and aviation fuel production multiplied several times.

item.title: CIS countries declare 2028 Year of Social Development and Quality of Life
item.description: The Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) has declared 2028 the Year of Social Development and Quality of Life, and 2029 the Year of Transport Connectivity. This decision was made at a meeting of CIS heads of state in Turkmenistan. The initiative aims to strengthen cooperation in social support and labor market development.

item.title: Kazakhstan Reduces Consumer Lending and Credit Fraud Significantly
item.description: Kazakhstan has reduced fraudulent loans by nearly fivefold over two years through measures limiting unsecured consumer lending. The Financial Market Regulator reports a near halving of credit portfolio growth rates. Stricter requirements for debt load ratios, a ban on loans with over 90 days overdue, and enhanced oversight are in place.

item.title: eGov Mobile App Serves Over 13 Million Users with More Than a Thousand Services
item.description: The eGov Mobile app has evolved into a unified digital platform with over 13.2 million users in seven years. Currently, it offers more than 1,100 state services and features, including digital documents and biometric identification, simplifying access to government services.

item.title: Kazakhstan Extends Mortgage Benefits for Vulnerable Citizens Until July 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan has extended the application deadline for additional mortgage assistance for socially vulnerable citizens to July 1, 2027. The financial support period is set until September 1, 2027. This extension provides more time for citizens facing payment difficulties to seek help, including potential debt relief or options to rent-to-own housing.

item.title: Kazakhstan Man Reports Attempted Abduction by Military Commissariat Staff in Astana
item.description: A resident of Astana reported being approached by two men claiming to be from the military commissariat, who attempted to take him away. The man stated he had a certificate proving his unsuitability for military service. He raised concerns about how the individuals knew his name and address, and they fled when he threatened to call the police.

item.title: Central Asia Agrees on New Water Limits for Amu Darya and Syr Darya
item.description: Central Asian countries have agreed on water withdrawal limits from the Amu Darya and Syr Darya for fall and winter 2026-2027. The agreement was reached at the Interstate Commission for Water Coordination meeting in Turkmenistan. While national limits were set, specific water allocations for each country remain undisclosed in the published meeting results.

item.title: Uzbekistan Explains Privatization Terms for 'Uzekspomarkaz' and International Cooperation Center
item.description: Uzbekistan's State Assets Management Agency Director explained the specific privatization terms for 'Uzekspomarkaz' and the International Cooperation Center. These entities, located in green zones of Tashkent, will be privatized under special conditions agreed upon with the Presidential Administration, aligning with the 'Green Zone' state program.

item.title: CIS Adopts Tajikistan's Proposal to Form a Positive Image of the Commonwealth
item.description: The CIS Heads of State adopted measures to create a positive image of the organization and its member states in the information space. Initiated by Tajikistan, the decision aims to develop coordinated approaches to prevent actions that could harm the reputation of the CIS and its participants, promoting responsible information policies.

item.title: Medieval Coins Found in Kyrgyzstan's Lake Issyk-Kul Offer Insights into Monetary History
item.description: Archaeologists have discovered 10th-11th century Karakhanid coins at the bottom of Lake Issyk-Kul, Kyrgyzstan. The coins, possibly high in lead due to copper shortages, are crucial for understanding medieval Central Asian monetary circulation. The discovery was made at the Toru-Aygyr archaeological complex, a submerged Silk Road settlement.

item.title: Kazakh Novel 'The Angel of Karaul' Presented at Frankfurt Book Fair, Highlights Nuclear Testing Impact
item.description: Roza Mukanova's novel 'The Angel of Karaul,' about a girl affected by Soviet nuclear testing near Kazakhstan's Semipalatinsk site, was presented at the Frankfurt Book Fair. The book explores the tragic consequences of the 1949-1989 nuclear tests on human health and the environment, focusing on the protagonist's isolation and search for acceptance.

item.title: Kazakhstan Conducts 208 Organ Transplants in First Nine Months of 2024, Aims for 310 Annually
item.description: Kazakhstan has performed 208 organ transplants in the first nine months of 2024, with a target of 310 annually by 2025. The Ministry of Health reported this on Europe's Organ Donation Day. The country has 11 transplant centers and is focusing on developing deceased donor programs to meet the needs of thousands of patients awaiting transplants.

item.title: Central Asian Cooperation Evolves from Five to Six Nations with Azerbaijan's Inclusion
item.description: Central Asian states' consultative meetings have become a key political platform, evolving from a 'five' to a 'six' with Azerbaijan's full participation. This expansion fosters new regional connections. Despite progress in trade and border agreements, challenges remain in institutional mechanisms, implementation gaps, water-energy issues, and inter-state competition.

item.title: Uzbekistan's $20 Million Solar Program Targets 3,100 Sites for Free Electricity
item.description: Uzbekistan's $20 million solar program, 'Yorqin Xonadon,' aims to equip 3,100 sites with free electricity systems, prioritizing Karakalpakstan. Implemented by the Ministry of Energy, Acwa, and China Southern Power Grid, it has already provided systems to 1,580 homes and 334 institutions, with more planned by May 2027.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Urges Regional Support for Afghanistan's Stability
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov called on regional nations to maintain support for Afghanistan, emphasizing that a stable country benefits the entire region. Speaking at a Central Asian leaders' meeting, he stressed the need for continued humanitarian aid and enhanced cooperation against terrorism, drug trafficking, and organized crime. Upholding commitments to Afghanistan is crucial for regional security.

item.title: UK Sanctions Third Kyrgyz Finance Ministry Company for Aiding Russia
item.description: The UK has imposed sanctions on Processing KG, a company affiliated with Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Finance. This marks the third such company to be sanctioned for allegedly assisting Russia. The sanctions highlight international pressure on entities perceived to be supporting Russia's economic activities.

item.title: Turkmenistan Imposes Strict Quarantine Measures at Border Crossing Amid Suspected Pneumonia Outbreak in Russia
item.description: Turkmenistan has reinstated strict COVID-19-like quarantine measures at the Garabogaz border crossing with Kazakhstan. Unconfirmed sources suggest this is due to a suspected pneumonia outbreak in Russia. Health officials are reportedly disinfecting the area and passengers, with some travelers being placed in quarantine.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Chair CIS Summit in Bukhara in 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan will chair the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) in 2027, with the CIS summit scheduled to be held in Bukhara on October 8-9. Turkmenistan and Azerbaijan will co-chair alongside Uzbekistan. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev outlined priorities including economy, new technologies, transport, security, education, science, and human potential development.

item.title: Tashkent's Specialized Genetic Dermatosis Department Marks Five Years of Rare Disease Care System Development
item.description: Tashkent's specialized genetic dermatosis department, the first in Central Asia, celebrates five years since its 2021 opening. Established with support from the Ministry of Health and the 'Kapalak Bolalar' fund, it has systematized medical care for rare skin conditions, now focusing on comprehensive family support.

item.title: First Caspian Ecological Summit Held in Turkmenistan's Avaza National Tourist Zone
item.description: The First Caspian Ecological Summit convened in Turkmenistan's Avaza National Tourist Zone on October 9, 2026. Presidents from Azerbaijan, Iran, Kazakhstan, and Russia participated. The summit focused on environmental protection and preserving the Caspian Sea's ecosystem, resulting in a heads of state decision. Turkmenistan advocates for cooperation within the UN framework for sustainable development and marine environment protection.

item.title: China's MFA: Stable Economic Ties with Europe Serve Mutual Interests
item.description: China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated that stable economic and trade relations between China and Europe are in the interest of both sides. The ministry hopes for aligned efforts and resolution of disagreements. Previously, China urged France and Germany to uphold open cooperation and free trade, warning against protectionism. China views economic interdependence as a path to open cooperation.

item.title: Uzbekistan Outlines Priorities for CIS Presidency in 2027, Focusing on Economy and Security
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced the country's priorities for its upcoming CIS presidency in 2027. Key areas of focus will include the economy, new technologies, transport, security, and education. Over 100 events are planned during Uzbekistan's chairmanship of the Commonwealth of Independent States.

item.title: Anorbank Board Member Resigns Amidst Shareholder Meeting and Rating Downgrade
item.description: Qahramonjon Olimov, a shareholder of Anorbank, has submitted his resignation from the bank's supervisory board. The issue will be discussed at a shareholder meeting on October 28. This follows a decision to issue additional shares worth 100 billion soums and a rating downgrade by Fitch Ratings due to uncertainties surrounding capital replenishment.

item.title: Houthi Attacks on Saudi Arabia's King Khalid Airport Leave Three Dead
item.description: Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation reported that Houthi attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh resulted in three fatalities and several injuries. The deceased were Saudi citizens, while the injured included individuals of various nationalities. The Houthis targeted the airport twice, damaging facilities and a Saudi Airlines aircraft.

item.title: State Assets Agency Denies Texnopark LLC Was Handed Over to Artel Management
item.description: The Director of the State Assets Management Agency, Sohibjon Murodov, refuted claims that Texnopark LLC in Tashkent was transferred to the management of the Artel group. He stated that the company's 100% state share belongs to the Tashkent city administration and has not been officially transferred to any private company.

item.title: Nearly 70,000 Cybercrimes Recorded in Uzbekistan in Nine Months
item.description: Uzbekistan recorded nearly 70,000 cybercrimes in the first nine months of the year, primarily involving the acquisition of citizens' funds through electronic payment systems. The Ministry of Internal Affairs reported that Meta companies respond to only 3% of requests to identify account owners.
